Remove `textDocument/formatting` from the request-method union so it can no longer be dispatched.
Remove any Zig AST-based formatting implementation (`std.zig.Ast` usage) that only existed to support formatting.
Ensure the server no longer advertises formatting capability (directly or indirectly).
Remove the `textDocument/didChange` branch that calls `@panic(...)`.
Choose and implement the minimal interim behavior: either (a) do not include `textDocument/didChange` in supported notification dispatch, or (b) keep it and handle it as a safe no-op.
Ensure the server stays running under common client behavior that may send `didChange` regardless of advertised sync.

summary: Add lifecycle state management and enforce protocol correctness
deliverables: Introduce a minimal lifecycle state machine with states: `uninitialized` → `initializing` → `initialized` → `shutting_down`.
On transport startup, enter the `uninitialized` state and begin a busy loop reading messages from stdin.
In `uninitialized` state, drop all notifications except `exit` (which terminates with code 1 per spec).
In `uninitialized` state, respond to any request other than `initialize` with error code -32002 (ServerNotInitialized).
When `initialize` request arrives, transition to `initializing`, process the request, send `InitializeResult` response.

After responding to `initialize`, remain in `initializing` state—must not send requests/notifications to client yet (except window/showMessage, window/logMessage, telemetry/event, $/progress with client's workDoneToken).
Client must not send additional requests/notifications until it receives `InitializeResult`.
When `initialized` notification arrives, transition to `initialized` state—server is now fully operational.
In `initialized` state, handle all supported requests and notifications normally.
When `shutdown` request arrives, transition to `shutting_down`, respond with `null` result.
In `shutting_down` state, respond to any request with error code -32600 (InvalidRequest) per spec.
In `shutting_down` state, drop all notifications except `exit`.
When `exit` notification arrives: terminate with code 0 if shutdown was received, code 1 otherwise.
Ensure the main loop is a proper busy loop that blocks on stdin and processes messages sequentially.
